as_told.title: Hal Puthoff is open to Wargo's confirmatory-feedback idea

plain: Eric Wargo, a writer on time and the mind, discussed Stargate, a US government programme from the 1970s to 1995 that tested remote viewing, the claimed ability to describe far-off places with the mind alone. Wargo suggests that what remote viewers really see may be the feedback they will be shown later, so they are glimpsing their own future. Podcast host Jesse Michels adds that Hal Puthoff, whom he calls the founder of the CIA's psychic spy programme, told him he was open to Wargo being right that such feedback is needed for it to work.
